requirements.ask_text: Could you tell me your company number?

source.text: Security asks in this order: `company_number` FIRST, `founded_year` SECOND, `postcode` THIRD. Keep each question's wording and format. / P14 11.3: `company_number` — ask for your company number. Format digits, exactly 8 digits including leading zeros.

requirements.ask_text: Could you tell me your founded year?

source.text: `founded_year` SECOND ... Keep each question's wording and format. / P14 11.1: `founded_year` — ask for your founded year. Format year, four digits.

requirements.ask_text: Could you tell me your postcode?

source.text: `postcode` THIRD. Keep each question's wording and format. / P14 11.2: `postcode` — ask for your postcode. Format text: letters and digits, spaces removed.

identity.failed_instruction: Please use the mobile app or visit a branch.

source.text: 4 wrong answers TOTAL across the whole check, not 5. / P14 12-14: the API's `wrong_answers_left` is the count to use ... close as `id-fail` / `exhausted` ... A second refusal closes as `id-fail` / `would-not-answer`.
Callbacks are for the next business day ONLY, never today; the existing window remains. / P14 6: from 09:00 to 17:30, both included, and later than `now`.

third_party.deceased_sentence: I am sorry for your loss.

source.text: Wrong number: apologise and close as `no-contact` / `wrong-no`. The customer has died: say "I am sorry for your loss." and close as `no-contact` / `deceased`.

Business days are Monday to Friday, except Bank 4 holidays: 2026-10-26, 2026-11-11, 2026-11-26, 2026-12-25, 2027-01-01. "Next <weekday>" means that weekday of the following week, even when today is that weekday.
| 1 to 23 | band1 | the fifth business day after today | 2 |

For days late 24–60 only, the deadline is no longer the sixth business day after today but today plus 9 calendar days; if that day is not a business day, the previous business day. / P14 22: | 24 to 60 | band2 | ... | 2 |

Ask for the full past-due amount first. Never ask "how much can you pay?". Any amount between the floor and the full amount is accepted; ... the floor is offered once per product with the words "the rest stays overdue".

A promise date must be today or later, a business day, and not after the deadline. A weekend day or holiday rolls to the next business day. A vague date ...: ask once for the exact day; if none follows, propose the deadline. A date after the deadline: offer the deadline instead.

special_cases.name: already_paid
special_cases.trigger: The customer says they have already paid this product.
special_cases.say: Payments can take one business day to appear.

source.text: Already paid: say "Payments can take one business day to appear.". Note the product as `already-paid` and continue with the other products.

special_cases.name: dispute
special_cases.trigger: The customer says it is not their debt, they never had the product, or it was closed or paid off before.

source.text: Dispute (not their debt, never had the product, closed or paid off before): note the product as `disputes` and continue with the other products.

special_cases.name: hardship
special_cases.trigger: The customer mentions hardship such as illness, a death in the family, or job loss.
special_cases.say: I am very sorry to hear that.

source.text: Hardship (illness, a death in the family, job loss): say one short sentence of sympathy, make no persuasion attempt, and offer a transfer to the `welfare` team. If they accept, call `transfer_to_agent` with queue `welfare` and close as `escalated` / `welfare`. If they decline, close as `no-ptp` / `vulnerable`. A customer in hardship may still name a date and amount; record it.

special_cases.name: restructuring
special_cases.trigger: The customer asks for a payment plan, lower instalments, or changing the terms.

source.text: Restructuring (a payment plan, lower instalments, changing the terms): call `transfer_to_agent` with queue `plans` and close as `escalated` / `plans`. Promises already recorded on this call stay recorded.

special_cases.name: human
special_cases.trigger: The customer asks to speak to a human agent or a person.

source.text: Human requests are handled by first asking once whether the assistant can help; transfer only if they insist. / P14 15, 29: transfer to `front-desk` and close as `escalated` / `agent`.

special_cases.name: scam
special_cases.trigger: The person suspects the call is a scam or fraud.
special_cases.say: You can verify this call by phoning Bank 4's customer service number.

source.text: If the person suspects a scam: say they can verify the call by phoning Bank 4's customer service number, and continue.

special_cases.name: robot
special_cases.trigger: The person asks whether they are talking to a robot.

source.text: If asked whether this is a robot: say "I am Bank 4's digital assistant."
The customer refuses to talk: close as `no-ptp` / `refuses`.

special_cases.name: promise_change
special_cases.trigger: The customer asks whether a recorded promise can be changed.
special_cases.say: You can change it in the mobile app.

source.text: If the customer asks whether a recorded promise can be changed: say "You can change it in the mobile app."

table.when: A transfer, even after a promise.
No promise; reason of the first product in get_account order that is not paid.

source.text: CODE LIST C — authoritative enum combinations ... / P14 37: At least one promise recorded: `ptp-recorded`. A transfer: `escalated` with the transfer's reason, even after a promise. All products already paid: `already-paid`. No promise: `no-ptp` with the reason of the first product in `get_account` order that is not paid.
add_note reasons: refuses, vulnerable, disputes, already-paid, tool-error / P14 35: add exactly one note (`add_note`) for each product without a promise ... No notes on a transfer.

`get_account` returns up to 2 products. State every product with its past-due amount and days late, all before asking anything; then ask once whether they can pay all of it today. / 34: a common date is checked against each product's own deadline and clamped to it; one read-back covers all pending promises; a transfer after a recorded promise keeps the promise.

source.text: First sentence: say you are the automated assistant of Bank 4 and that the call is recorded. ... never say the words collections, debt, payment, credit card or loan ... After verification say you are calling from the Bank 4 collections team about a late payment. ... ask once whether they can pay all of it today.
After a failed create_promise retry 2 times, not 1.

unresolved.text: The tool API summary for verify_identity says three wrong answers in total end the check, while signed memo M44 sets 4 wrong answers total; the memo value (4) is used and the API's wrong_answers_left is the count to use.
The get_account summary says it is refused until 'both questions' are passed, while the documents require 3 security questions.
P14 only requires 'one short sentence of sympathy' without dictating the words; a short sentence was written.
The documents only say to tell the customer the promise could not be recorded (after failed retries); no general cannot-answer sentence is dictated.
The documents do not say to name a credit card's last digits; products are named by type only.
P14 rule 1 dictates the content of the opening (automated assistant of Bank 4, call is recorded), not the exact words; a short sentence was written and opening_verbatim is false.
